Asturian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /fuˈtuɾo/ [fuˈt̪u.ɾo]
  • Rhymes: -uɾo
  • Syllabification: fu‧tu‧ro

Adjective

[edit]

futuro

  1. neuter of futuru

Esperanto

[edit]
Esperanto Wikipedia has an article on:
futuro
Wikipedia eo

Etymology

[edit]

From Italian futuro, French futur, English future, German Futur, all ultimately from Latin futūrus, irregular future active participle of sum (“to be”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰuH- (“to become, be”). Compare similar IAL derivations like Ido futuro, Interlingue futuro, Volapük fütür.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /fuˈturo/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -uro
  • Syllabification: fu‧tu‧ro

Noun

[edit]

futuro (accusative singular futuron, plural futuroj, accusative plural futurojn)

  1. (uncountable) future (the time ahead)
    Synonym: estonteco
  2. (countable, grammar) future tense

Derived terms

[edit]
  • futurismo
  • futurologio
  • futurologo

See also

[edit]
  • -os

Further reading

[edit]
  • “futuro”, in Plena Ilustrita Vortaro de Esperanto [Complete Illustrated Dictionary of Esperanto], 2020, →ISBN
  • “futuro”, in Reta Vortaro [Online Dictionary] (in Esperanto), 1997-present

Galician

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin futūrus (“about to be”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /fuˈtuɾo/ [fuˈt̪u.ɾʊ]
  • Rhymes: -uɾo
  • Hyphenation: fu‧tu‧ro

Adjective

[edit]

futuro (feminine futura, masculine plural futuros, feminine plural futuras)

  1. future

Noun

[edit]

futuro m (plural futuros)

  1. the future
  2. (grammar) future tense

Ido

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Spanish futuro, Italian futuro, English future, French futur and German Futur.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /fuˈtu.ro/

Noun

[edit]

futuro (plural futuri)

  1. future (period that yet has to happen)
    • 1911, Progreso, volume 3, page 454:
      Ni rimarkas ica opiniono : « La futuro apartenas, nek a la panslavismo, nek a la pangermanismo, nek a la panlatinismo, ma a l'Unionita Stati di Europo ».
      (please add an English translation of this quotation)
  2. (grammar) future tense (tense used for future events)

Antonyms

[edit]
  • pasinto

Derived terms

[edit]
  • futurala

Interlingua

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

futuro (plural futuros)

  1. future (time posterior to the present)

Antonyms

[edit]
  • passato

Italian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin futūrus (future participle of esse).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /fuˈtu.ro/
  • Rhymes: -uro
  • Hyphenation: fu‧tù‧ro

Adjective

[edit]

futuro (feminine futura, masculine plural futuri, feminine plural future)

  1. future
    Synonym: venturo
    Antonym: passato
  2. soon-to-be
    Synonym: presto

Noun

[edit]

futuro m (plural futuri)

  1. the future
    Synonym: avvenire
  2. (grammar) the future tense
    Hyponyms: futuro semplice, futuro anteriore

Derived terms

[edit]
  • futuro anteriore
  • futuro semplice

Related terms

[edit]
  • futuribile
  • futurismo
  • futurista
  • futuristico
  • futurologia

Further reading

[edit]
  • futuro in Treccani.it – Vocabolario Treccani on line, Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana

Latin

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

From futūra +‎ -ō.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [fʊˈtuː.roː]
  • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [fuˈtuː.ro]

Verb

[edit]

futūrō (present infinitive futūrāre, perfect active futūrāvī, supine futūrātum); first conjugation (Medieval Latin)

  1. to postpone, throw into the future

Portuguese

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /fuˈtu.ɾu/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /fuˈtu.ɾu/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /fuˈtu.ɾo/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /fuˈtu.ɾu/

  • Audio (Portugal (Porto)):(file)
  • Rhymes: -uɾu
  • Hyphenation: fu‧tu‧ro

Etymology 1

[edit]

Borrowed from Latin futūrus (“about to be”).

Adjective

[edit]

futuro (feminine futura, masculine plural futuros, feminine plural futuras)

  1. future
    Synonym: vindouro
Derived terms
[edit]
  • futuramente
Related terms
[edit]
  • futuração
  • futurar
  • futurismo
  • futurista
  • futurologia
  • futurólogo
  • futuroso

Noun

[edit]

futuro m (uncountable)

  1. future (the time ahead)
    Synonyms: destino, porvir, posteridade
    Antonym: passado
    • 1999, Jane Katra, Russell Targ, O coração da mente, Editora Cultrix, →ISBN, page 92:
      É difícil ler sobre o trabalho dessas pessoas e não se convencer da realidade da precognição, mesmo que não se entenda como ela se dá. A descoberta mais importante dos dados combinados — partindo de dezenas dessas experiências de precognição de muitos laboratórios em todo o mundo — é que não é mais difícil ver mediunicamente o futuro do que ver mediunicamente acontecimentos ocultos no presente. Esse é o mistério que nos cativa.
      (please add an English translation of this quotation)
  2. (grammar) future tense
Coordinate terms
[edit]
  • (future tense): pretérito, presente
Derived terms
[edit]
  • sem futuro

Etymology 2

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

futuro

  1. first-person singular present indicative of futurar

Spanish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Latin futūrus.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /fuˈtuɾo/ [fuˈt̪u.ɾo]
  • Audio (Colombia):(file)
  • Rhymes: -uɾo
  • Syllabification: fu‧tu‧ro

Adjective

[edit]

futuro (feminine futura, masculine plural futuros, feminine plural futuras)

  1. future (occurring in the future)

Noun

[edit]

futuro m (plural futuros)

  1. future (the time ahead)
    Synonym: porvenir
    Antonym: pasado
    • 2012 July 26, “Google anuncia el internet del futuro”, in CNN en Español‎[2]:
      Si el usuario es aprobado en el preregistro, podrá decidir qué paquete desea, y se programará en una fecha futura su instalación, agregó la compañía, que no ofreció una fecha para el arranque del servicio.
      (please add an English translation of this quotation)
  2. (grammar) future, future tense
    Synonym: tiempo futuro
    Antonym: pasado

[edit]

  • futurista
  • futurístico

  • futuro de subjuntivo
  • futuro imperfecto
  • futuro perfecto
  • futuro simple
  • futuróloga
  • futurología
  • futurólogo
  • hipotecar el futuro
